newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to release last 53 Golden Venture migrants.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to release last 53 Golden Venture migrants.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it planned to release 53 Chinese migrants who have been held in detention since 1993, when they swam ashore from the freighter that smuggled them to New York and then ran aground.

The White House, which announced the decision in a brief statement, said the 53 were expected to be released by March 1. Whether they will be allowed to remain in the United States will depend on decisions of U.S. immigration courts, it added.

The group was the last of about 300 Chinese citizens smuggled to the United States on board the Golden Venture freighter, which ran aground on a Queens, New York, beach in June 1993. Most of the rest were settled in Latin American countries or returned to China.
The 300 had braved a treacherous sea journey, held in stark holds filled with clothing, garbage and other debris, only to swim for their lives when the ship ran aground.

At the time, the United States decided to keep them in custody to discourage others from making similar journeys. Previously such migrants had been released, but many did not show up at their immigration hearings held six months later.

"The administration's policy of detaining smuggled aliens has deterred smuggling by organized criminal syndicates, resulting in a sharp decrease in the number of alien smuggling vessels that have reached U.S. shores," the White House said.
It added that newly enacted immigration legislation had significantly strengthened the government's ability to deter such smuggling.

"Under these circumstances, and weighed against the exceptional and unusual length of detention of the Golden Venture migrants, the administration has concluded that their parole from detention is appropriate," it added.
